doc.name: quantifyme
doc.instructions: QuantifyMe turns a trading strategy written in plain English into a backtested signal model for seven FX pairs. Each session gets an anonymous trial account automatically, with a small credit allowance; `link_account` connects an existing QuantifyMe account instead. `one_shot` takes the user's request as `prompt` (plus optional `symbol` and `timeframe`) and starts one deploy per call; each call creates a separate deploy and deploy card. The platform routes the request itself: a vague request ('deploy a 15min EURUSD model') deploys the best curated preset for that market, or a fresh build when there is none; a specific rule-based description ('buy when RSI < 30') generates a fresh strategy. A community strategy is another user's code: it deploys only after the user has seen its author and code (`get_strategy_code`) and picked it, by passing its `community_id` to `one_shot`. `one_shot` returns a `job_token` at once; `get_deploy_result(job_token)` waits for the deploy to finish and returns the out-of-sample stats, the live dashboard URL and the code source as text. Its `source` field says whether the code came from a curated preset, a fresh generation or a community strategy (with its author); a `suggestion` is a matching community strategy that was not deployed. `get_model_chart` returns a model's trades and stats for a chart. `list_models` and `list_deployed` show the account's models; `browse_community` and `find_strategy` search published community strategies; `get_quote` returns the latest price. QuantifyMe never places orders or moves money: it sends signals to the channels the user sets up (Telegram, email, Discord or webhook; the free plan and trial keys get Telegram, email and in-app; Discord and webhook need a paid plan), and `one_shot` sets up Telegram from `telegram_chat_id` or a webhook from `webhook_url`. Backtests and signals are information, not financial advice; no performance is promised.

tools.name: one_shot
tools.title: Deploy Strategy (generate + backtest + go live)
tools.description:
End-to-end deploy: generate strategy → train → deploy live.

    One of `prompt` (free-form NL), `preset` (curated winning strategy), or
    `community_id` (copy a published community strategy) is required. If more
    than one is passed, precedence is community_id > preset > prompt.

    Args:
      prompt: Natural-language strategy description (e.g. "Buy when RSI < 30, sell > 70").
      symbol: Currency pair to backtest on. One of: EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD,
        USDCHF, USDCAD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD. Default EURUSD.
      timeframe: Candle granularity. One of: 1min, 5min, 15min, 1h. Default 15min.
      claude_model: Which Claude variant writes the code: "sonnet" (default, best
        quality) or "haiku" (faster, cheaper). Generation is billed from the
        account's credits. Ignored when `preset` is set (no generation needed).
      preset: Curated winning-strategy slug. Skips Claude generation entirely
        — deploys a pre-saved strategy known to backtest well on the chosen
        symbol. Available slugs: ema_cross_fast, momentum, scalper_stack,
        sma_only, trend_ema, volatility, bb_squeeze, all_mix, pivot_kid_ema.
        Not every slug exists for every symbol; list_models shows what deployed.
      community_id: Copy-trade a published community strategy. Pass the `id`
        of an entry from `browse_community`. Loads that exact strategy code,
        skips Claude generation, then trains + deploys it. `symbol`/`timeframe`
        still apply to the backtest+deploy.
      webhook_url: Optional webhook to receive live signals.
      telegram_chat_id: Optional Telegram chat ID for signal delivery.

    Returns at once (the deploy runs in the background so the live card can
    stream progress) with:
        - job_token (str): get_deploy_result(job_token) returns the final result.
        - poll_url (str): the progress URL the live card polls.
        - pending (bool): true; the deploy is still running.
        - symbol, timeframe (str).

    Each call starts one deploy and one deploy card, and is billed from the
    account's credits. The server routes the request: a vague `prompt` deploys
    the best curated preset for the market, or a fresh build when there is none;
    specific rules generate a fresh strategy. A community strategy deploys only
    after the user has seen its author and code (get_strategy_code) and picked
    it, through its `community_id`.

    get_deploy_result(job_token) waits for the deploy and returns the
    out-of-sample stats, `stem`, `live_url` and `source`/`author` as text; its
    `source` says when a pre-existing community strategy was used, and a
    `suggestion` is a matching community strategy that was not deployed.

_meta.openai/widgetDescription: A live-deployed QuantifyMe model: live progress, then backtest chart (candles + buy/sell arrows + trades) + a one-click live link.

tools.name: get_deploy_result
tools.title: Get Deploy Result
tools.description:
Wait for a `one_shot` deploy to finish and return its final result as text.

    Takes the job_token `one_shot` returned. Waits until the deploy finishes, up
    to about 2.5 minutes; past that it returns ok:false with pending:true, and a
    later call with the same token picks the same deploy up again. It renders no
    card of its own: the one_shot deploy card is the visual, where the client
    renders it.

    `source == "community"` means the deploy used a pre-existing strategy by
    `@author` that the user picked. A `suggestion` is a community strategy that
    matched a vague request and was not deployed; it deploys only after the user
    has seen its author and code and picked it.

    Args:
      job_token: the token returned by `one_shot`.

    Returns:
      dict with: ok, stem, model, live_url, symbol, timeframe, channels (list),
      stats:{ret, wr, pf, n, mdd} (out-of-sample test-split metrics), source
      ("preset" | "generated" | "community"), author (community username if any),
      author_url + strategy_url (links for the author and the community strategy),
      community_id, suggest_custom (bool), suggestion ({community_id, title,
      author} or null: matched, not deployed), and note (a one-line summary of
      the source). On failure: {ok:false, error} (or {pending:true}).

tools.name: link_account
tools.title: Link My QuantifyMe Account
tools.description:
Link this chat to the user's existing QuantifyMe account.

    For a user who already has a QuantifyMe account, who wonders why their
    models are missing here, or who wants what they deploy here to show up in
    their own dashboard.

    By default this connector works with NO signup: it mints an anonymous trial
    account per MCP session, so models deployed here belong to that throwaway
    identity rather than to the user's real one. This returns a short-lived URL;
    once the user opens it and approves, every later call that carries the same
    OAuth bearer or the same MCP session acts as their account and deploys land
    in their own model list. A client that opens a new MCP session on every turn
    must link again in that session; every answer's `acting_as` line says which
    identity was used.

    Returns `link_url` and `link_code`: show the user both. They open the link,
    sign in, type the code on the QuantifyMe page and approve; the code only
    works for this chat. If the session is already linked, returns
    already_linked:true and the account's username instead.

tools.name: list_models
tools.title: List Trained Models
tools.description:
List the user's trained models with pre-computed train/test stats.
    `acting_as` names the identity listed: the linked account or a trial user (#1962).

tools.name: generate_strategy
tools.title: Generate Strategy Code (no training)
tools.description:
Generate Python strategy code only: nothing is trained or deployed.

    Returns the generated code for the user to read or edit; each call is billed
    from the account's credits.

    Args:
      features: Plain-English description of features (e.g. "RSI 14, Bollinger Bands").
      signals: Plain-English description of signal logic (e.g. "Buy when RSI < 30").
      model: ML model name (default Random Forest).
      risk: Plain-English risk rules (e.g. "0.5% stop loss").
      description: Optional one-line summary; the generator weighs it as the
        main request.
      symbol: Currency pair the code should target. One of: EURUSD, USDJPY,
        GBPUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD. Default EURUSD.
      timeframe: Candle granularity. One of: 1min, 5min, 15min, 1h. Default 15min.
      claude_model: "sonnet" (default) or "haiku" (faster, about a third of the credits).

tools.name: browse_community
tools.title: Browse Community Strategies (leaderboard)
tools.description:
Browse the public community leaderboard of published strategies, ranked
    by a composite performance score (best first). No signup or key needed.

    Each entry's `id` is what `one_shot` takes as `community_id` to deploy a
    live signal model running that exact strategy.

    Args:
      limit: How many top entries to return (default 20, max 200).
      sort: Ranking metric, best-first — one of "composite" (default),
        "ret" (total return), "wr" (win rate), "sharpe", "n_trades". Mirrors
        the quantifyme.ai/community page's sortable columns. The sorted
        entries keep their `id`, which one_shot(community_id=...) deploys.

    Returns:
      dict with:
        - scripts (list[dict]): ranked entries, best first. Each has:
            id (int — pass to one_shot as community_id), username, title,
            description, created_at, score, and metrics {total_ret,
            sharpe_strat, win_rate, n_trades, mdd, profit_factor}.
        - count (int).
        - metric (str): the sort key applied.

_meta.openai/widgetDescription: Top community trading strategies, each with a one-click copy-and-deploy.

tools.name: find_strategy
tools.title: Find a Matching Strategy
tools.description:
Find a published community strategy that matches a plain-English idea.

    Mirrors the quantifyme.ai landing page: "Found <X> by @<author> (WR/PF):
    use it, or generate fresh". It is for browsing; a vague deploy request is
    handled by one_shot(prompt=...) alone, which deploys the best curated preset
    or a fresh build. A community strategy is another user's code, so it deploys
    only after the user has seen its author and code (get_strategy_code with the
    match's community_id) and picked it. The two outcomes:
      - use the match: one_shot(community_id=<match.community_id>) deploys that
        exact strategy, with no generation;
      - generate fresh: one_shot(prompt="<their description>") writes a new
        custom strategy.
    With no match, only the second applies.

    Args:
      description: the user's strategy idea in plain English (e.g. "buy EURUSD
        15min when RSI < 30, sell when RSI > 70").
      symbol: optional pair to constrain the match (EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD,
        USDCHF, USDCAD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD).
      timeframe: optional granularity to constrain the match (1min/5min/15min/1h).

    Returns:
      dict with:
        - match: the best existing strategy, or null. When present:
            {community_id, title, username, wr, pf, ret, n_trades, symbol,
             timeframe}. Pass community_id to one_shot to deploy it unchanged.
        - description: echoed back; one_shot(prompt=...) with it generates fresh.
        - suggestion: one sentence describing the match and the two outcomes.

tools.name: get_strategy_code
tools.title: Get Community Strategy Code
tools.description:
Get the actual Python code behind a community leaderboard strategy.

    Takes an entry's `id` from `browse_community` or `find_strategy` and returns
    its real `feature_engineering()` + `strategy_config()` source, for the user
    to inspect or tweak. The same id passed to `one_shot` as `community_id`
    deploys it unchanged. Read-only, no signup needed.

    Args:
      community_id: The `id` of a community entry (from `browse_community`).

    Returns:
      dict with: id, title, username, description, symbol, timeframe,
      metrics {total_ret, win_rate, profit_factor, n_trades, mdd, sharpe_strat},
      and `code` (the full Python source).

tools.name: get_quote
tools.title: Get Current Price (G7 FX quote)
tools.description:
Get the latest price for a G7 FX pair — a quick "what's it at now" check.

    Useful for context before deploying a strategy. The price is the close of
    the most recent 1-minute bar from the platform's market feed (not a raw
    live tick); FX markets close on weekends, so the `stale` flag marks a bar
    that is more than 15 minutes old.

    Args:
      symbol: G7 pair — one of EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD, AUDUSD,
        NZDUSD. Default EURUSD.

    Returns:
      dict with: symbol, price (latest close), time (bar timestamp, UTC),
      change + change_pct (vs the prior 1-min bar), stale (bool).

tools.name: get_model_chart
tools.title: Show Backtest Chart (equity + trades)
tools.description:
A trained model's backtest: trades, stats and the data for a cumulative-return chart.

    Takes a model's `stem` (from `get_deploy_result`, `one_shot` or `list_models`)
    and returns how it traded. In clients that render the openai/outputTemplate
    widget (ChatGPT) it shows an interactive chart; elsewhere the structured
    output carries the trades and stats a client can draw as a line chart of
    the cumulative return and a trade table.

    Args:
      stem: The model stem (e.g. "14_EURUSD_15min_Model_24") from `list_models` / `one_shot`.

    Returns:
      dict with: ok, stem, symbol, timeframe, stats {ret, wr, pf, n, mdd, sharpe},
      and trades [{type, entry_time, exit_time, entry_price, exit_price, pnl,
      pnl_pct, exit_reason, period}] (most recent ~200). exit_reason is one of
      TP / SL / close_only / signal / end. ret/mdd/wr are fractions; pnl_pct is percent.

_meta.openai/widgetDescription: A model's backtest: interactive price chart with buy/sell arrows + trade log + win-rate/profit-factor stats.
